rule.description: One class keeps several independently evolving responsibilities on mutually disconnected instance-state groups at god-class scale (>= 3 responsibility islands, >= 10 own behavior methods, >= 6 instance attributes).

checks.description: Detect classes whose own behavior methods split into three or more mutually disconnected responsibility islands (connected components of the method <-> instance-attribute graph) at god-class scale.
checks.detected_relation: class -> several disjoint instance-state responsibility groups each with dedicated behavior methods
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A class centralized around several independently evolving duties keeps each duty on its own state group, so no non-constructor method bridges them: the class has many reasons to change while a cohesive class shares its state and stays one island at any size.

matches.evidence: Token-emission island of the god class: state {clear, contents, stack} is used only by the token loop and its stack helpers (_analyze_lexemes, _push, on_top, pop); covered by the class-level entry because these methods predate the centralization.

Vocabulary island: state {_word_fixes} (a per-object copy of the packaged spelling-alias table seeded from it at construction) is touched only by _collect_word_fixes and _correction_for; unreachable from the token core.

Program-boundary protocol island: state {_program_protocol} (opening word plus closing phrase) is touched only by _expect_opening and _expect_closing; analyze() delegates to them but touches no state with them, so the island stays separate from the token core.

Source-provisioning island: state {_source_lines, _source_path} (staged raw program text and its origin path) is touched only by _read_source and _inline_source; the token loop reads the copied contents attribute instead.

Debug-report island: state {_dump_ready, _trace_stem, debug} is touched only by record_lexemes and record_parse_tree, which author the CLI's evidence files; this duty was moved in from the driver class.

excluded.reason: Larger class, but its methods all revolve one shared responsibility (building the AST from the token stream via the shared stack state), so it stays one island and does not match.
Two-method driver below the scale thresholds; the reporting duty it lost is part of this case only through its counterpart entry in modiscript/lexer.py.
Static helpers own no instance state, are excluded from island construction by definition, and remain available under their original names for compatibility.
Flask routes are thin consumers of the driver's public execute; no class there approaches the rule's relation.
